rv.q: It deals with a spendthrift hero who, fawned on when his credit is good, is rejected when poor and retreats into misanthropic isolation. It appears a perfect parable for our times, which is exactly what it becomes in Nicholas Hytner's exhilarating production featuring a compelling central performance by Simon Russell Beale.
Simon Russell Beale is a masterful Timon, all back-slapping bonhomie at the start but fearsome in the depths of his misanthropic misery.
